fluff.overview:
The Pueblo class surveillance DropShip was a specialized intelligence platform built for the Star League Defense Force. At 8,400 tons, this Aerodyne was designed to hide in plain sight among civilian traffic while conducting covert surveillance operations within the territorial borders of Star League member states. Each vessel featured one of at least a dozen different exterior configurations designed to mimic common civilian craft.

Conceived when modified civilian vessels proved capable of gathering intelligence but incapable of defending themselves, and when the alternative Bug-Eye class proved too expensive and contained overly classified technology, the Pueblo filled a critical niche. Its crews operated under deep cover, rarely wearing uniforms and engaging in legitimate interstellar trade to maintain their civilian disguise while traveling through and monitoring member state activities.
fluff.capabilities:
The Pueblo carries a well-rounded weapons array suited to self-defense rather than offensive operations. The nose mounts two ER PPCs, two ER large lasers, three Artemis-equipped LRM-15 racks, and two medium lasers. Each broadside carries two ER PPCs, two ER large lasers, two Artemis-equipped LRM-15s, two medium lasers, and an additional ER PPC in the rear firing position. The aft arc mounts two ER PPCs, two ER large lasers, two Artemis-equipped LRM-15s, and two medium lasers. One hundred sixty-four double heat sinks manage the thermal load across all arcs.

The vessel's defining feature is its mobile HPG, allowing it to transmit intelligence directly without requiring a JumpShip relay. A naval communications scanner suite and look-down radar complement the HPG, providing comprehensive surveillance capability. Computer surveillance systems are housed in cargo containers designed to survive customs inspection. Four small craft bays carry shuttles that double as boarding craft for the embarked marine detachment. With 1,576 tons of cargo space, the vessel maintains a convincing civilian trading profile. The atmo_flyer quirk reflects superior atmospheric handling characteristics that help maintain the impression of a commercial vessel, and the imp_com quirk reflects its enhanced communications suite. Armor totals 1,860 points of ferro-aluminum protection.
fluff.deployment: The Pueblo operated exclusively with the Star League Defense Force's intelligence services, conducting covert surveillance missions within the borders of member states. Crews maintained civilian identities and engaged in legitimate commerce to preserve their cover. Following the fall of the Star League, surviving Pueblos were lost during the Succession Wars as their irreplaceable systems degraded beyond repair.
fluff.history:
House Cameron recognized that maintaining the Star League's peace required constant awareness of each member state's activities. Stationing a WarShip within a state's borders would spark an interstellar scandal, so the SLDF needed a specialty craft that could operate covertly. Early attempts using modified civilian ships succeeded in gathering intelligence but left the vessels defenseless when discovered. The Bug-Eye class offered capability but at astronomical cost, and its highly classified technology made losses unacceptable.

The Pueblo was created as the practical solution, entering service around 2673. Each vessel shared identical internal capabilities but wore one of many different exterior shells to pass as various civilian craft types. The crews, all SLDF personnel, maintained deep cover identities and participated in genuine interstellar commerce. Even the surveillance systems were housed in cargo containers that could survive customs inspections without revealing their true purpose.

Following the Amaris Coup, not all Pueblo class vessels accompanied General Kerensky on the Exodus. Those that remained in the Inner Sphere were eventually identified and destroyed during the Succession Wars, as their sophisticated systems could not be maintained without Star League-grade support infrastructure. No Pueblo class vessels are known to have survived into the modern era.
